data.title: MDQ Specification Audit: essay
data.scope: The essay question type: `docs/question-types/essay.md` and `schema/essay.yaml`, read against `docs/references/grammar.md`, `docs/references/patterns.md`, `docs/question-types/question-base.md`, `docs/exam.md` and `docs/responses.md`. Earlier audits already settled the shared rules.

data.title: Contradictions
Ambiguities
Omissions
Inconsistencies
Grammar violations
Schema mismatches
Essay grammar rejects an indented [essay] tag and trailing spaces
data.snippet: essay : "[essay]"
data.description: The rule has no `ws?` before or after the tag. Tested with Lark: `  [essay]`, `   [essay]`, `\t[essay]` and `[essay]  ` are all rejected. But question-base.md:219-220 says "a tag may be indented", and grammar.md:59-69 defines the leading `ws?` of a block as the CommonMark indentation of at most three spaces. The numeric and short-answer tag rules (numeric.md:75, short-answer.md:154) start with `ws?` and end with `ws?`; the essay rule does not. mdq-py accepts `  [essay]`, `   [essay]` and `[essay]  ` as essay bodies, and rejects `    [essay]` (code block), which matches the prose, not the grammar.
data.impact: A reader who follows the grammar rejects valid documents with an indented tag or trailing spaces; an implementation built from the grammar disagrees with mdq-py.
data.fix: Write the rule as `essay : ws? "[essay]" ws?`, as the numeric and short-answer rules do.

data.title: Essay grammar does not say it applies to a paragraph, so it accepts the content of a list item
data.snippet: Body consists of a single `[essay]` tag.
data.description: The grammar matches only the text `[essay]` and does not state the block that holds it. grammar.md:73-79 says a list-item grammar applies to the item content after the removal of the marker. With that reading, the content of `* [essay]` is `[essay]` and the grammar accepts it, while the Additional Rules table (essay.md:90) forbids the tag as a list item (`foreign-choice-marker`). The content of the heading `## [essay]` is also `[essay]`. mdq-py reads only a paragraph as the tag: `* [essay]` gives `foreign-choice-marker` and `## [essay]` gives a missing body. The grammar also does not say that the tag is the whole paragraph: `Describe the Pantanal.\n[essay]` (one paragraph) is rejected by mdq-py, and the spec settles this only by the word "single".
data.impact: The block context of the tag comes from implementation behavior and a footnote, not from the grammar.
data.fix: State that the rule is the whole content of a paragraph, for example `essay_block : ws? "[essay]" ws? nl` with a sentence that the block is a paragraph, and that a list item or heading is not the tag.

data.title: Answer key heading has no grammar; setext and spacing variants are unspecified
data.snippet: It starts with an `H2` heading with the text `## [answer-key]`
data.description: The answer key section is defined only in prose; essay.md has no rule for it, unlike the `## [extra]` section of ordering (ordering.md:146: `"##" ws "[" "extra" "]" nl+ content`). The prose says both "an H2 heading" and "the text `## [answer-key]`", so it does not settle these inputs: the setext H2 `[answer-key]` + `---` (mdq-py accepts it as the answer key), `##   [answer-key]   ` (mdq-py accepts), `## [Answer-Key]`, `### [answer-key]` and `## [answer-key] Notes` (mdq-py rejects them as `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue). The prose also does not say where the section ends: mdq-py puts a later `## Sub` heading and its paragraphs inside `answerKey`.
data.impact: Two implementations can split the same document into a different epilogue and answer key.
data.fix: Add a grammar rule for the section, for example `answer_key : "##" ws "[" "answer-key" "]" ws? nl md_block+`, and state whether a setext H2 is accepted and that the section runs to the end of the document.

data.title: SLUG accepts `essay`, so `[essay]` at the start of the first paragraph is a slug
data.description: The slug rule (question-base.md:174-175, 197-199) reads a bracket at the start of the first paragraph as a slug when its content matches SLUG, and `essay` matches. No rule excludes the type tag names. So `[essay] Describe the Pantanal.` followed by `[essay]` is a question with id `essay` (mdq-py output: `{"type": "essay", "id": "essay", ...}`). A document whose first paragraph is only `[essay]` is either a slug-only stem paragraph or the body with no stem; the spec does not say which (mdq-py reads it as the body and reports a missing field).
data.impact: Contrived inputs where the spec gives two readings of the same bracket.
data.fix: State whether a type tag name such as `essay` can be a slug, and that a paragraph of only `[essay]` is always the essay tag.

data.text: The essay tag literal `"[essay]"` agrees with the bracketed-tag rules of question-base.md:211-217: tested with Lark, it accepts `[essay]` and rejects `[ essay ]` (whitespace inside brackets), `[Essay]` (case), `[essay] write here`, `[essay]\nwrite here` (more than a single tag) and `[essay](http://x)` (a link). mdq-py gives the same result for each of these inputs.

data.title: The response format of a "text" essay is not defined
data.snippet:
"text" indicates that the response should be a rich text input, potentially
supporting markdown or other formatting.
data.description: `input: text` asks for a rich text editor "potentially supporting markdown or other formatting", and `docs/responses.md:38` says the essay response is "the text the student wrote". Neither document says what the response string holds for a rich text editor: Markdown source, HTML, or text with the formatting removed. `input: code` and `input: plain` have no such doubt.
data.impact: Two hosts that exchange responses (an LMS, a grader, an exporter) can store the same answer as Markdown in one and as HTML in the other. A renderer cannot tell which it received, and raw HTML in a response is also an injection risk when the host renders it as Markdown.
data.fix: State in `docs/responses.md` and in Input that the response of every essay is a string, and that for `input: text` it is CommonMark source. A host whose editor produces HTML converts it before it stores the response. `plain` and `code` responses are verbatim text.

data.title: The extent and content of the answer key section are not specified
data.snippet:
The answer key section is placed below the `[essay]` tag and any existing
epilogue block. It starts with an `H2` heading with the text `## [answer-key]`
data.description:
The text says where the section starts but not where it ends or what it may hold. mdq-py reads every block up to the end of the question, headings included: `## [answer-key]` followed by `Text.` and `## Rubric` gives `answerKey: "Text.

## Rubric

- a"`. The text also does not say whether the heading may carry text after the tag (`## [answer-key] Rubric` is rejected as a `forbidden-block-element` of the epilogue) or whether another level (`### [answer-key]`) opens the section (also rejected as a heading in the epilogue). Inside an exam the end of the section is the next `===` or `---` block, which the text does not mention. Compare `docs/question-types/ordering.md:186-213`, which defines its sections in more detail.
data.impact: An author cannot know if a rubric with its own headings belongs to the answer key, and a second implementation can stop the section at the next heading or at the next H2.
data.fix: State that the section is the H2 heading `## [answer-key]` alone on its line (the `ws` rules of bracketed tags apply), and that it holds every block after the heading up to the end of the question (end of file, or the next block in an exam). Any block is valid inside it, headings included except H1. Add a grammar rule for it next to `essay`.

data.title: An empty or repeated answer key section has no documented rule
data.snippet: | answerKey | error    | blank-text                   | if defined, must have at least one visible character       |
data.description: The Additional Rules table has no rule for a second `## [answer-key]` section, but `examples/invalid/essay-two-answer-keys.mdq.md` expects a `parse-error`. For a section with no content (`## [answer-key]` as the last line), the `blank-text` rule suggests an error, but mdq-py accepts the document and drops the field: the result has no `answerKey` and no error.
data.impact: The corpus enforces a rule the spec does not state, and an empty section, which is almost always an unfinished question, passes with only the `missing-answer-key` info at most.
data.fix: Add the rules to the table: at most one answer key section (`parse-error`), and an answer key section with no visible character is `blank-text`, as for a defined field. Add a corpus example for the empty section.

data.title: The text never maps the answer key section to the `answerKey` field
data.snippet: ## Answer key
data.description: The Answer key section describes the Markdown syntax but never states that its content becomes the `answerKey` field of the AST, nor how the blocks are joined into the string. The field name appears only in the Additional Rules table (lines 92 and 95) and in `schema/essay.yaml:41`. The document also has no YAML form of a parsed essay.
data.impact: A reader of the Markdown spec cannot tell which field holds the answer key, or that it is a field of the body and therefore invalid in the frontmatter (`invalid-frontmatter-field`).
data.fix: Add one sentence: the blocks of the section, without the heading, are the `answerKey` string, with the same normalization license as `stem` and `epilogue`. Add the YAML form of the example.

data.title: The Grading section does not give the score range, automation or response
data.snippet: Essay questions are graded manually.
data.description: The rules that apply to an essay are spread over other documents: the automation is `manual` (`question-base.md:280`), every response is pending (`responses.md:312-313`), the score is in [0, 1] (`exam.md:359`), the exam `grading` does not apply (`exam.md:359`), and the response is a string (`responses.md:190-204`). The essay document links to none of them, and the instructor's score range is stated only for fill-in blanks (`responses.md:320-321`). `ordering.md` has Automation and Response sections; essay does not.
data.impact: A reader of the essay document cannot learn how an essay is scored or what its response looks like without reading three other documents.
data.fix: Expand Grading: the automation is `manual`, every response is pending until the instructor gives a score in [0, 1], the exam `grading` does not apply and `penalty` does. Add a Response section that links to `responses.md`.

data.title: The rules of the `[essay]` paragraph are not stated
data.snippet: Body consists of a single `[essay]` tag.
data.description: The text does not say that the tag must be alone in its paragraph, that the tag is case-sensitive, or what a second `[essay]` is. The corpus fixes all three: `essay-tag-with-text` (`[essay] com no máximo 200 palavras`) and `essay-tag-uppercase` (`[Essay]`) expect `parse-error`, and `essay-two-tags` expects `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue. None of these is in the Additional Rules table.
data.impact: Only the corpus defines these behaviors, so an implementation written from the text can accept trailing text as part of the tag or read `[Essay]` as the body.
data.fix: State that the body is a paragraph whose only content is `[essay]`, with optional `ws` around it, written in lowercase, and that a later `[essay]` paragraph is a forbidden element of the epilogue. Add the parse errors to the table, as other types do.

data.title: A warning rule is written as "must"
data.snippet: | highlight | warning  | ignored-highlight            | must be omitted unless `input` is "code"                   |
data.description: The level is `warning`, which maps to SHOULD, but the rule says "must be omitted". Footnote 1 says only that the property is ignored, with no requirement level. `question-base.md` writes its warnings as "should" (`unsafe-id`: "should be url-safe").
data.impact: The table contradicts its own level, and a reader can take the rule as an error.
data.fix: Write "should be omitted unless ..." in both tables, and in footnote 1 add that the property SHOULD be omitted.

data.title: When the answer key may be shown to students is not defined
data.snippet:
key section is optional and serves as a guide for the instructor to grade the 
responses and may be presented as feedback to the students.
data.description: The answer key "may be presented as feedback", but the text does not say when (after the response, after grading, after the exam closes) or whether a host must hide it before. The other types define feedback that shows after grading; a pending essay "shows no feedback" (`responses.md:319-320`).
data.impact: A host can show the model answer while the exam is open, and the rule that a pending response shows no feedback seems to forbid showing it at all until the instructor grades.
data.fix: State that the answer key MUST NOT be shown to the student before they submit the response, and that it MAY be shown after, even while the response is pending.

data.title: No fields for response size or attachments
data.snippet: | input     | string  | Either "code", "text" or "plain"[^2]      |
data.description: Essay has no field for a minimum or maximum length (words or characters), the size of the input box, or file attachments. Moodle essay questions have `responsefieldlines`, `minwordlimit`, `maxwordlimit` and `attachments`; the `mdq export` targets lose nothing today, but an import from Moodle drops them.
data.impact: Authors write length limits in the stem (`essay-tag-with-text` shows the attempt), where no host can enforce them.
data.fix: Decide whether MDQ covers these. If yes, add optional `minWords`/`maxWords` fields; if no, state that limits belong in the stem or in `meta`.

data.title: The answer key section has no grammar, and its heading variants and extent are not specified
data.description: The answer key section is defined only in prose; essay.md has no rule for it, unlike the `## [extra]` section of ordering (ordering.md:146: `"##" ws "[" "extra" "]" nl+ content`). The prose says both "an H2 heading" and "the text `## [answer-key]`", so it does not settle these inputs: the setext H2 `[answer-key]` + `---` (mdq-py accepts it as the answer key), `##   [answer-key]   ` (mdq-py accepts), `## [Answer-Key]`, `### [answer-key]` and `## [answer-key] Notes` (mdq-py rejects them as `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue). The prose also does not say where the section ends or what blocks it may hold: mdq-py reads every block up to the end of the question, so a later `## Rubric` heading and its list are inside `answerKey`. Inside an exam the end is the next `===` or `---` block, which the text does not mention.
data.fix: Add a grammar rule, for example `answer_key : "##" ws "[" "answer-key" "]" ws? nl md_block+`. State that the heading is an ATX H2 alone on its line (decide on the setext form; CommonMark reads both as H2), and that the section holds every block after it, headings included except H1, up to the end of the question (end of file, or the next block in an exam).

data.description: The grammar matches only the text `[essay]` and does not state the block that holds it. grammar.md:73-79 says a list-item grammar applies to the item content after the removal of the marker. With that reading, the content of `* [essay]` is `[essay]` and the grammar accepts it, while the Additional Rules table (essay.md:90) forbids the tag as a list item (`foreign-choice-marker`). The content of the heading `## [essay]` is also `[essay]`. mdq-py reads only a paragraph as the tag: `* [essay]` gives `foreign-choice-marker` and `## [essay]` gives a missing body. The grammar also does not say that the tag is the whole paragraph: `Describe the Pantanal.\n[essay]` (one paragraph) is rejected by mdq-py, and the spec settles this only by the word "single". The corpus fixes more cases that the Additional Rules table does not list: `essay-tag-with-text` (`[essay] com no máximo 200 palavras`) and `essay-tag-uppercase` (`[Essay]`) expect `parse-error`, and `essay-two-tags` expects `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue.
data.fix: State that the body is a paragraph whose only content is the rule, for example `essay_block : ws? "[essay]" ws? nl`, and that a list item or heading is not the tag. State that a later `[essay]` paragraph is a forbidden element of the epilogue, and list the parse errors in the Additional Rules table, as other types do.

data.description: The rule has no `ws?` before or after the tag. Tested with Lark: `  [essay]`, `   [essay]`, `\t[essay]` and `[essay]  ` are all rejected. But question-base.md:219-220 says "a tag may be indented", and grammar.md:59-69 defines the leading `ws?` of a block as the CommonMark indentation of at most three spaces. The numeric and short-answer tag rules (numeric.md:75, short-answer.md:154) start with `ws?` and end with `ws?`; the essay rule does not. mdq-py accepts `  [essay]`, `   [essay]` and `[essay]  ` as essay bodies, and rejects `    [essay]` (code block), which matches the prose, not the grammar. The `ordering` rule (ordering.md:141) has the same gap; the ordering audit covers it.

data.methodology:
The audit script `scripts/spec_audit.py` passed all 15 steps before the audit started: it compiles every Lark snippet, checks the Additional Rules tables against `docs/lint-codes.md` and the corpus, and checks the frontmatter tables against the schemas.

The lead auditor read `docs/question-types/essay.md` with the shared specs and recorded contradictions, ambiguities, omissions and inconsistencies. The audit focused on what is specific to essay: the `[essay]` tag, the `input` and `highlight` fields, the answer key section, the response and the manual grading. Edge cases were run through mdq-py to see how the reference implementation reads the text.

One subagent turned the essay grammar and the shared grammar into Lark and tested what they accept and reject. A second, independent subagent scanned the essay document and schema, ran each complete example through `mdq validate`, and checked the Additional Rules table against the MUST, SHOULD and MAY requirements of the text.

data.title: Essay spec does not say where the answer key ends or which blocks it may hold
data.snippet:
The answer key section is placed below the `[essay]` tag and any existing
epilogue block. It starts with an `H2` heading with the text `## [answer-key]`
data.description:
The spec gives only the start of the section. It does not say that the section runs to the end of the question, or that the forbidden elements of question-base.md (H1, a paragraph or heading that starts with `[`) do not apply to it. mdq-py takes every block up to the end of the question as the answer key, with no check: `## [answer-key]

Key.

[essay]` gives `answerKey: "Key.

[essay]"`, a following `## Rubric` heading and an H1 are kept in the answer key, and text after the answer key that an author means as epilogue goes into the answer key too. No example in examples/ has a heading, a bracketed paragraph or a second `[essay]` after the answer key.
data.impact: A second implementation can stop the section at the next H2, or apply the epilogue rules to it, and read the same document differently. Text meant for students can end up in the hidden answer key.
data.fix: State that the answer key holds every block from its heading to the end of the question, and whether the forbidden-element rules apply to it. Add examples for the decided cases.
data.conditions: An essay with an `## [answer-key]` section followed by a heading, a bracketed paragraph or more prose.

data.title: Essay spec does not say which heading forms open the answer key
data.snippet: epilogue block. It starts with an `H2` heading with the text `## [answer-key]`
data.description: The text says both "an `H2` heading" and "the text `## [answer-key]`". It does not say if a setext H2 (`[answer-key]` over `---`), an ATX heading with closing hashes (`## [answer-key] ##`), an indented heading, an H3, a different case (`## [Answer-Key]`) or text after the tag (`## [answer-key] model`) open the section. mdq-py accepts the setext, closing-hash and indented forms as the answer key, and rejects H3, the uppercase form and trailing text with `forbidden-block-element` on the epilogue. No example in examples/ covers any of these forms.
data.impact: Implementations can disagree on whether a document has an answer key, which changes what students see.
data.fix: Define the heading in the grammar (for example only an ATX H2 with the exact tag, as ordering.md does for its sections) and add invalid examples for the other forms.
data.conditions: An answer key heading written in a form other than `## [answer-key]`.

data.title: An empty `## [answer-key]` section is neither defined nor a blank-text error in the essay spec
data.snippet: | answerKey | error    | blank-text                   | if defined, must have at least one visible character       |
data.description: The rules say a defined but blank answerKey is a `blank-text` error. The spec does not say whether an `## [answer-key]` heading with no block after it defines an answer key. The corpus decides that it does not: examples/valid/essay/empty-answer-key.mdq.md is valid and only gives `missing-answer-key`, while examples/invalid/model-only/essay-blank-answer-key.yaml is a `blank-text` error. This rule is only in the corpus.
data.impact: An implementation that follows the text can report `blank-text` for the empty section, and reject a document the corpus accepts.
data.fix: State in the Answer key section that a heading with no visible content after it defines no answer key, and that `blank-text` applies only to the YAML/JSON form.
data.conditions: A Markdown essay with `## [answer-key]` as its last line.

data.title: Essay Grading section does not give the score range, the pending state or how weight and penalty apply
data.snippet: Essay questions are graded manually.
data.description: The Grading section is one sentence. The rules that apply to an essay are spread in other files: the automation is `manual` (question-base.md:279-280), every response is pending and has no score until the instructor gives one (responses.md:310-319), the score is in [0, 1] and the exam `penalty` applies (exam.md:359), and the exam `grading` does not apply. essay.md links to none of them. Also no example in examples/grading/ grades an essay, so the pending behavior has no test case.
data.impact: A reader of essay.md cannot find the score range of a manual score or that an exam scorer must report the response as pending.
data.fix: Add Grading and Automation text that states these rules and links to them, and add an essay grading example that shows a pending response.
data.conditions: Grading an essay alone or in an exam.

data.title: Essay spec does not say when the answer key may be shown to students
data.snippet: responses and may be presented as feedback to the students.
data.description: The answer key "may be presented as feedback to the students", but essay.md has no Feedback section and does not say when. responses.md:318-319 says a pending response shows no feedback, and every essay response is pending until the instructor scores it. The spec does not say whether the answer key can be shown after the instructor scores the response, after the exam closes, or never by default.
data.impact: A host can show the model answer before grading ends, which leaks it to other students in the same exam.
data.fix: Add a Feedback section that states when the answer key MAY be shown, consistent with the pending rule of responses.md.
data.conditions: An essay with an answer key in a host that shows feedback.

data.title: Essay spec does not define the response content for `input: text`
data.snippet:
"text" indicates that the response should be a rich text input, potentially
supporting markdown or other formatting.
data.description: For `input: text` the editor is "rich text", "potentially supporting markdown or other formatting". responses.md gives the essay response only as "the text the student wrote", a string. The spec does not say if the string of a rich text response is Markdown, HTML or text with no formatting, or if `plain` and `code` responses differ in shape.
data.impact: Two hosts can store the same rich text answer as Markdown and as HTML, and a response from one cannot be read by the other.
data.fix: State the format of the response string for each `input` value (for example Markdown for `text`, verbatim text for `plain` and `code`).
data.conditions: An essay with the default `input: text`.

data.title: Essay spec says both that essays may require and that they always use manual grading
data.snippet: Essay questions are usually open-ended, and may require manual grading.
data.description: Line 55 says essays "may require manual grading", which implies some are graded automatically. Line 82 and question-base.md:280 say essays are always graded manually (`manual` automation).
data.impact: A reader can expect some automatic grading of essays, for example from the answer key.
data.fix: Replace "may require manual grading" with a statement that every essay response is graded by the instructor.

data.title: Essay places its answer key section after the epilogue, ordering places its sections before it
data.snippet:
The answer key section is placed below the `[essay]` tag and any existing
epilogue block.
data.description: Both types use `## [name]` sections after the body. In essay the epilogue comes before `## [answer-key]` (examples/valid/essay/epilogue-and-answer-key.mdq.md). In ordering the sections follow the content block directly and the epilogue comes after the last section; prose between the block and a section is a `parse-error`. question-base.md:4-6 and 264-265 describe the essay order (special sections after the epilogue), so ordering disagrees with the base, and the two types disagree with each other.
data.impact: Authors must learn two placements for the same `## [name]` construct, and a parser cannot share the section logic.
data.fix: Choose one placement for `## [name]` sections relative to the epilogue and use it in question-base.md, essay.md and ordering.md.
data.conditions: An essay or ordering question with both an epilogue and a section.

data.title: Essay `input` and ordering `content` hold the same code/text choice under different names
data.snippet: | input     | string  | Either "code", "text" or "plain"[^2]      |
data.description: Both fields select between `code` (paired with `highlight`, with the same `ignored-highlight` and `unknown-highlight-language` rules) and `text`. Essay calls the field `input` and adds `plain`; ordering calls it `content` and has no `plain`. The lint-codes.md row of `ignored-highlight` has to say "`input`/`content`".
data.impact: Authors who write both types must remember two names for one concept.
data.fix: Use one field name for the code/text choice in both types, or document why they differ.

data.title: Essay doc lacks the Feedback, Automation and Response sections of the other types
data.snippet: ## Grading
data.description: ordering.md has Feedback, Grading, Automation and Response sections; short-answer.md has Grading, Automation and Feedback; the choice types have Feedback and Grading. essay.md has only Answer key and a one-sentence Grading. It also has no section that documents the `answerKey` field: the field appears only in the Additional Rules table, and nothing in prose maps `## [answer-key]` to `answerKey`.
data.impact: Readers cannot find essay rules where they find them for the other types.
data.fix: Add Feedback, Automation and Response sections, and state that `## [answer-key]` sets the `answerKey` field.

data.title: Essay rules table uses "must" for a warning-level rule, and two rules are not in the prose
data.snippet: | highlight | warning  | ignored-highlight            | must be omitted unless `input` is "code"                   |
data.description: question-base.md:349-354 maps warning to SHOULD, but the `ignored-highlight` rule says "must be omitted". The prose (essay.md:24, 44-45) says only that `highlight` is ignored and never says that it SHOULD be omitted. `code-input-without-highlight` (info) is not in the prose either. The same "must" wording is in ordering.md:339.
data.impact: The level in the table and the requirement word disagree.
data.fix: Write "should be omitted" in the table and add SHOULD/MAY sentences for the two rules in the Input section.

data.title: Exam rules about `---` and setext headings do not cover the essay answer key
data.snippet:
Inside an exam, the epilogue of a question MUST NOT use `---` as a thematic
break.
data.description: The exam rules name only the epilogue (and the stem and instructions for `setext-heading`). The answer key comes after the epilogue and is the last block of an essay in an exam, so a `---` in it has the same problem. mdq-py applies the epilogue rule to it: a `---` in the answer key gives `parse-error` with the message "a question's epilogue cannot use '---'", and a setext `[answer-key]` heading gives `setext-heading` at path `epilogue` while it parses as `answerKey`. The spec does not state either behavior and no example in examples/ covers it.
data.impact: Implementations can accept a `---` in an answer key, and a later question then starts inside it.
data.fix: Extend the exam rules to every block after the body, the answer key included.
data.conditions: An essay with an answer key inside an exam.

data.title: Essay spec does not say how footnotes resolve across the stem, epilogue and answer key
data.snippet: The answer key section is placed below the `[essay]` tag and any existing
data.description: Each part is stored as its own Markdown string. mdq-py accepts a stem with `[^1]` whose definition is in the answer key: the stem keeps a reference with no definition, and the definition is hidden with the answer key. The spec does not say if a footnote reference must be defined in the same field, and no example in examples/ covers it (examples/valid/essay/epilogue-starts-with-footnote.mdq.md only has an epilogue footnote).
data.impact: The student view renders a dangling footnote, or a host that renders the whole document shows text from the answer key.
data.fix: State that a footnote definition belongs to the field it is in, and lint a reference defined in another field.
data.conditions: An essay that uses footnotes and has an answer key.

data.title: Essay has no way to declare a response length limit
data.snippet: | highlight | string  | Programming language of "code" inputs[^1] |
data.description: The frontmatter has only `input` and `highlight`. There is no field for a minimum or maximum length (words or characters) and no rule for attachments. examples/invalid/essay-tag-with-text.mdq.md (`[essay] com no máximo 200 palavras`) shows that authors want to declare a limit, and today they can only write it in the stem.
data.impact: A host cannot enforce or show a length limit from the document.
data.fix: Decide if MDQ supports length limits or attachments; if so, add OPTIONAL fields, otherwise state that they are out of scope.

data.title: schema/essay.yaml gives `highlight` a validation role the spec does not have
data.snippet:
Programming language used for syntax highlighting and, where
          supported, validation.
data.description: The schema says `highlight` is used for syntax highlighting "and, where supported, validation". essay.md:44-45 says only that it specifies the language for syntax highlighting. The spec does not define any validation of the response by language.
data.impact: Hosts can reject responses that do not compile, which the spec does not permit or describe.
data.fix: Remove the validation clause from the schema, or describe the behavior in essay.md.

data.title: schema/essay.yaml rejects an empty `highlight`, the spec does not say so
data.snippet: minLength: 1
data.description: The schema sets `minLength: 1` on `highlight`, so `highlight: ""` is a `schema-error` (mdq-py confirms). essay.md does not state this constraint; question-base.md:366-367 says identifiers and syntax fields reject the empty string, but essay.md does not say that `highlight` is one.
data.impact: Readers of essay.md cannot tell that an empty `highlight` is an error and not an ignored value.
data.fix: Add the constraint to the essay frontmatter table or footnote [^1].

reason: Duplicate of F8 (answerKey mapping), F9 (Automation/Response sections) and F12 (feedback)

data.description: The answer key section is defined only in prose; essay.md has no rule for it, unlike the `## [extra]` section of ordering (ordering.md:146: `"##" ws "[" "extra" "]" nl+ content`). The prose says both "an H2 heading" and "the text `## [answer-key]`", so it does not settle these inputs: the setext H2 `[answer-key]` + `---` (mdq-py accepts it as the answer key), `##   [answer-key]   ` (mdq-py accepts), `## [Answer-Key]`, `### [answer-key]` and `## [answer-key] Notes` (mdq-py rejects them as `forbidden-block-element` in the epilogue). The prose also does not say where the section ends or what blocks it may hold: mdq-py reads every block up to the end of the question, so a later `## Rubric` heading and its list are inside `answerKey`. Inside an exam the end is the next `===` or `---` block, which the text does not mention. The forbidden elements of question-base.md are not checked in the section either: mdq-py keeps an H1 and a second `[essay]` paragraph after the answer key as answer key text (`answerKey: "Key.\n\n[essay]"`), and prose after the answer key meant as epilogue goes into it. No example in examples/ has a heading, a bracketed paragraph or more prose after the answer key, or any heading form other than `## [answer-key]`.

The Additional Rules table has no rule for a second `## [answer-key]` section, but `examples/invalid/essay-two-answer-keys.mdq.md` expects a `parse-error`. For a section with no content (`## [answer-key]` as the last line), the `blank-text` rule suggests an error, but mdq-py accepts the document and drops the field: the result has no `answerKey` and no error. The corpus already decides the empty case the other way: examples/valid/essay/empty-answer-key.mdq.md is valid and expects only `missing-answer-key`, while examples/invalid/model-only/essay-blank-answer-key.yaml is a `blank-text` error. So the rule that an empty Markdown section defines no answer key exists only in the corpus.

The level is `warning`, which maps to SHOULD, but the rule says "must be omitted". Footnote 1 says only that the property is ignored, with no requirement level. `question-base.md` writes its warnings as "should" (`unsafe-id`: "should be url-safe"). The info rule `code-input-without-highlight` (essay.md:94) is not described in the prose either.

data.text: The essay corpus covers the tag variants and misplacements: spaced, uppercase, NBSP-indented, indented, in a list, in a blockquote, with trailing text, repeated, and an answer key before the body or repeated.
schema/essay.yaml agrees with essay.md on the `input` enum and its default `text`, on `highlight` being ignored with a warning for non-code input, and on `answerKey` blank-text.

The essay lint codes in essay.md agree with docs/lint-codes.md in name, level and scope (`ignored-highlight`, `unknown-highlight-language`, `code-input-without-highlight`, `missing-answer-key`, `foreign-choice-marker`).
Both complete examples in essay.md (lines 7-11 and 63-78) validate with mdq-py with no error or warning.

data.snippet: The body consists of a single `[essay]` tag.

data.fix: Add a rule for a second section (`parse-error`) to the table. For the empty section, two readings are defensible: (a) an empty section is an absent answer key, reported only as `missing-answer-key`, as the corpus decides (examples/valid/essay/empty-answer-key.mdq.md); (b) it is a defined but blank field, `blank-text`, as for `title:` with only spaces. Recommended: (a), since `## [answer-key]` with nothing after it is a common template placeholder, and state it in the text and the table.

data.text: Essay looks like the simplest type, but most of its rules live in the corpus and in mdq-py, not in the text: the tag paragraph, the answer key section, its extent and its empty form.
The response of a rich text essay has no defined format, so two hosts can exchange the same answer as Markdown and as HTML.

data.title: [Spec] Define the `[essay]` paragraph and the `## [answer-key]` section in the grammar
data.summary: The essay grammar is one literal, and the answer key section has no grammar at all. What the tag paragraph is, how the answer key heading is spelled, where the section ends, what an empty or repeated section is, and which field it fills are known only from the corpus and mdq-py. Recommended: write `essay_block` and `answer_key` rules, state that the section runs to the end of the question and fills `answerKey`, document an empty section as an absent answer key (corpus behavior), a second section as `parse-error`, and that a footnote belongs to the field it is in. Decide whether a setext `[answer-key]` heading is valid (recommended: yes, as CommonMark reads it as H2) and whether type tag names can be slugs (recommended: yes, and a paragraph of only `[essay]` is always the tag).
acceptance: essay.md has grammar rules for the tag paragraph and the answer key section
The text states the extent of the section and that it fills `answerKey`
The Additional Rules table lists the second-section and tag-paragraph errors
The corpus has examples for a section with headings inside and for the empty section

data.title: [Spec] Define the response format of a "text" essay
data.summary: `input: text` is a rich text editor, but neither essay.md nor responses.md says whether the response string is Markdown, HTML or plain text. Options: (a) CommonMark source for `text`, verbatim text for `plain` and `code`; (b) leave it to the host. Recommended: (a), since MDQ is Markdown and a host with an HTML editor can convert.
acceptance: responses.md and essay.md state the format of the response for each `input`
A corpus response example exists for an essay

data.title: [Spec] Document essay grading, response and answer key visibility in essay.md
data.summary: The essay Grading section is one sentence. The automation, the pending state, the [0, 1] score range, the exam `grading` exclusion and the response shape live in three other documents, and the text does not say when the answer key can be shown. Recommended: add Automation and Response sections as ordering has, and state that the answer key MUST NOT be shown before the student submits and MAY be shown after, even while pending. Also decide whether MDQ covers response length limits (recommended: no; state that they go in the stem or `meta`).
acceptance: essay.md has Grading, Automation and Response sections with links to responses.md and exam.md
The text states when the answer key may be shown

data.title: [Spec] Use one placement for `## [name]` sections relative to the epilogue
data.summary: Essay puts its answer key after the epilogue; ordering puts its sections right after the body and the epilogue after them. The exam rules about `---` and setext headings name only the epilogue, although mdq-py applies them to the answer key. Options: (a) sections always after the epilogue, as question-base.md describes; (b) sections always right after the body. Recommended: (a), since it agrees with question-base.md and the essay corpus; ordering then follows in its own audit. Extend the exam rules to every block after the body.
acceptance: question-base.md, essay.md and ordering.md state the same placement
exam.md applies the `---` and setext rules to the answer key
A corpus exam example has an essay with an answer key

data.title: [Spec] Use one field name for the code/text choice of essay and ordering
data.summary: Essay `input` and ordering `content` select the same `code`/`text` mode, with the same `highlight` rules. Options: (a) keep both and document why (essay describes the editor, ordering describes the lines); (b) rename one. Recommended: (a), since the meanings differ (`plain` exists only for an editor) and a rename breaks documents; add one sentence to each document.
acceptance: essay.md and ordering.md explain the relation between `input` and `content`, or one field is renamed with a changelog entry
